svg.title: Theories of Cognitive Development
svg.desc: Stage theories of development compared on one age axis: Piaget's four stages; Case's sensorimotor, interrelational, dimensional and vectorial stages; Fischer's tiers of skill levels, which climb in steps that take longer and longer; Kegan's orders of consciousness; and Erikson's eight psychosocial crises. Ladders show Commons's orders of hierarchical complexity, Loevinger's ego stages and Bach's levels of lucidity. Panels show Vygotsky's zone of proximal development, Case's account of working memory, Carey's Quinian bootstrapping, and patterns the theories share.
